what_it_does.name: expo-dev-client
what_it_does.summary: Instructions for building, installing and using Expo development clients, builds of an app that bundle expo-dev-client for testing native code changes on physical devices. They set up a development profile in eas.json, build with EAS Build in the cloud with submission to TestFlight, or locally into .ipa, .apk or .aab files, install the builds on simulators and devices, and connect the client to the Metro bundler. Use it when an app needs local Expo modules, Apple targets, third-party native modules not in Expo Go, config plugins, or testing of remote push notifications and App or Universal Links.
tasks: decide whether a development client is needed instead of Expo Go
configure a development profile in eas.json
build an iOS dev client in the cloud and submit it to TestFlight
build dev clients locally for iOS and Android
install local builds on a simulator, an iOS device or an Android device
check build status and connect the dev client to Metro
launch the dev client without onboarding, dev menu or Tools button

risks.risk: A changed or compromised release of @expo/agent-cli runs on the machine, since the feedback command fetches the latest version with npx --yes and no pinned version.
Instructions placed in user-provided text reach the feedback command, since that text is passed to it as an argument.
risks.mitigation: none stated, C2 judges it a standard ingestion point for a reporting tool

risks.risk: A cloud build uses paid EAS build minutes and a paid Apple Developer account when the agent builds or distributes through EAS Build or TestFlight.
risks.mitigation: building locally is free, no confirmation step stated

risks.risk: Task details and project context leave the machine to Expo when the agent submits a feedback report, which the files ask for after repeated failures or user intervention.

limitations: Installing an iOS build on a device requires signing.
Device and TestFlight distribution needs a paid Apple Developer account.
Expo CLI skips the onboarding sheet and dev menu only on SDK 58+ and only for launches it starts from a non-interactive shell.

known_problems.workaround: rebuild with eas build -p ios --profile development --clear-cache

known_problems.problem: errors, misleading or outdated information in the skill
